title: Support offline artifact mirror endpoints (registries + chart repos) for on-prem Private
author: Bruno Silva
release_notes:
- Terraform modules now support configuring offline artifact mirrors for on-prem/air-gapped Private deployments (registry, chart repo, and optional OS package mirrors).
- Adds validation to prevent partial/misconfigured mirror settings and improves error messages.
- Updates docs and examples for air-gapped installation workflows.
body:
## Summary
On-prem/air-gapped customers need to pull all Redwood Private artifacts from internal mirrors (OCI registry, Helm chart repo/OCI charts, and sometimes OS package mirrors) rather than the default public endpoints. This PR adds first-class Terraform inputs to configure those mirror endpoints across the Private modules, plus validation so we fail early with actionable errors.

This is intended to pair with installer-side bundle verification and upgrade tooling work; Terraform should make it easy to pin and route all artifact resolution to the right internal endpoints.

## Motivation / context
- Design partners requested a supported way to use offline registries and chart mirrors (no direct internet egress from cluster nodes).
- Support escalations have shown that partial configuration (e.g., registry mirror set but chart repo still public) leads to brittle installs and confusing failures.

## What changed
1) New mirror configuration variables
- Adds an `artifact_mirrors` input (module-level) that can configure:
  - Container registry mirror for Redwood images
  - Helm chart repo mirror OR OCI chart registry mirror
  - Optional OS package mirrors used by the on-prem bootstrap (where applicable)
- Keeps `artifact_source` / version pinning behavior intact; this PR only affects *where* artifacts are fetched from.

2) Validation + guardrails
- Validates mirror URLs (scheme, host, no trailing whitespace), and enforces required combinations.
- Prevents ambiguous configuration:
  - If `helm_charts.mode = oci`, require `helm_charts.oci_registry` and disallow `helm_charts.http_repo_url`.
  - If `helm_charts.mode = http`, require `helm_charts.http_repo_url` and disallow `helm_charts.oci_registry`.
- Adds clear remediation messages (example values + where the mirror is expected to be reachable from).

3) Provider wiring and module outputs
- Wires mirror endpoints into the places we configure:
  - Helm provider repository/registry settings
  - Kubernetes image references for system components where we template image strings
  - Optional outputs that expose the resolved endpoints for support bundles / operator visibility

4) Docs and examples
- Updates module READMEs and `examples/onprem-airgapped/`:
  - Shows a full working config using an internal registry (`registry.company.lan/redwood/*`) and a chart mirror.
  - Adds notes on TLS, custom CAs, and DNS constraints.

## Usage example
```hcl
module "redwood_private" {
  source  = "redwoodinference/private/redwood"
  version = "~> 0.42"

  private_version = var.private_version

  artifact_mirrors = {
    container_registry = {
      endpoint = "registry.company.lan"
      namespace = "redwood"
    }

    helm_charts = {
      mode = "http" # or "oci"
      http_repo_url = "https://charts.company.lan/redwood"
      # oci_registry = "registry.company.lan/charts"
    }
  }
}
```

## Backward compatibility
- Existing installs that do not set `artifact_mirrors` are unchanged.
- The validations are scoped to only apply when the new inputs are set.

## Testing
- `terraform validate` across root modules
- `terraform test` (where available in CI)
- Local plan/apply against a kind-based harness using a fake registry endpoint (docs note this is a connectivity check only; actual pulls happen in-cluster)

## Follow-ups
- Add an explicit preflight check in the installer for mirror reachability from within the cluster network (Terraform can’t verify that reliably).
- Consider adding a helper module for uploading/publishing the on-prem bundle into the mirror endpoints (out of scope here).

Refs: PM-826 (design partner beta readiness), ENG-4821 (Private upgrade plan foundation)

modules/onprem: support helm chart mirror modes (http vs oci) and registry endpoint overrides
validation: enforce required mirror fields + improve error messages
docs: add air-gapped mirror configuration guide + update examples
outputs: expose resolved artifact endpoints for operator visibility
conversation:
Fatima Noor (review): Can we clarify whether we support both chart repo (HTTP) and OCI charts? Air-gapped customers will likely prefer OCI.
Bruno Silva (author): Yes. Added `helm_charts.mode` with explicit validation to avoid mixed configs. Updated docs with both examples and guidance on choosing.

Irene Choi (review): The registry endpoint and namespace mapping is easy to misconfigure. Can we surface the final resolved image path somewhere for support?
Bruno Silva (author): Added outputs `resolved_container_registry` + `resolved_image_prefix` and documented where they show up in the rendered values.

Hanae Suzuki (security): For internal mirrors using private CAs, we need to be explicit about trust chain. Terraform can’t fix that, but docs should mention it.
Bruno Silva (author): Added a doc section on custom CAs, cluster node trust store, and Helm registry auth/TLS notes.

Victor Alvarez (networking): Please call out DNS expectations (mirror must resolve from worker nodes / in-cluster). Also avoid assuming `.lan`.
Bruno Silva (author): Updated docs to state 'resolvable from cluster network' and removed `.lan` wording outside examples.

Connor O'Brien (release eng): Any chance validations break existing users? Also: can we keep error messages copy/pastable.
Bruno Silva (author): Validations are gated on `artifact_mirrors` being set. Updated errors with explicit example values and single-line strings for copy/paste.

Fatima Noor: Approved.
Irene Choi: Approved.
Connor O'Brien: Approved (after CI rerun).
